title: Save manually before every choice
body:
The game autosaves often, but the autosave can land after the choice. Make a **manual save** before an important conversation or before starting a job: if you don't like the outcome, reload and try another option.

You can save from the menu almost any time you are not in combat.

title: Your attributes can be redistributed
body:
A build is not final: from the character menu you can **refund perks** and **reset attributes** to spend them again.

Try whatever you like and adjust once you find weapons or cyberware you prefer.

title: You are locked in Watson until The Heist
body:
During Act 1 you can only explore **Watson**: the district is closed off for Saburo Arasaka's visit to Konpeki Plaza. Watson does not close later; it is the other way round: **you are locked inside Watson until The Heist**, and the rest of Night City opens in Act 2. Watson stays reachable after that.

- Since 2.0, **all enemies scale to your level**: difficulty no longer depends on the district.
- Loot and vendor stock also scale with your level.
- Watson's five ripperdocs, the Cyberpsycho Sightings, many of Regina's gigs and the NCPD Scanner Hustles are already within reach.

Use this stretch to level up and gear up before The Heist: afterwards the story keeps you away from shops for a good while.

title: Start The Heist around level 10
body:
No source gives a recommended level for The Heist, and enemies scale with you, so you do not need to be over-levelled. Even so, you should start it **around level 10**:

- Level 10 unlocks **Tier 2 cyberware**: Reinforced Tendons, Optical Camo and the Biotech Σ cyberdeck. Tier 2 weapons arrive from level 9.
- **Intelligence 9** opens Hack Queue and the Embedded Exploit branch.
- Memory Boost (from level 5) and Optical Camo are already on sale.
- The Heist is long, and what follows, Love Like Fire and Playing for Time, gives you no shopping stops.

To get there, do the five Act 1 Cyberpsycho Sightings and Regina's low-tier gigs: they give XP and eddies. **Save manually before you go in**: there are missable weapons inside.

title: Cyberpsychos and Regina's gigs
body:
**Cyberpsycho Sightings (Psycho Killer):** they start with Regina's call after The Ripperdoc and Jackie's talk in The Ride. Act 1 has **five in Watson**: Demons of War (after The Pickup), Lt. Mower, Six Feet Under, Ticket to the Major Leagues and Where the Bodies Hit the Floor. The sixth Watson one, Bloody Ritual, needs Act 2, from 8 PM to 5 AM. **Incapacitate them instead of killing them** for Regina's better reaction; the reward comes either way.

**Regina's gigs:** Watson has 23, tiers 1 to 8 (the gig's difficulty, not your level). Start with the tier 1 ones: Hippocratic Oath, Many Ways to Skin a Cat, Monster Hunt, Playing for Keeps and Rite of Passage. Since 1.5 they need no Street Cred. It is not confirmed which ones appear before The Heist: some may wait for Act 2.

Finishing all the Watson gigs triggers Last Call, which leaves the **Axolotl** in your stash. Its Tier 5 needs level 33: finish them very early and you get a lower tier.

title: Making eddies in Watson
body:
- **Sell junk and loot you don't use** at Drop Points (Sell All Junk) and at vendors. Since 2.0 loot scales with your level.
- **Access points:** Breach Protocol gives eddies; the Advanced Datamine also gives quickhacks and crafting specs.
- **NCPD Scanner Hustles** (blue map markers): short fights that pay well.
- **Cyberpsycho Sightings:** per game8, Psycho Killer pays €$33,270 in total, and it recommends it at levels 10 to 25.
- **Regina's gigs:** Last Login, for example, pays €$6,400.

If Royce died in The Pickup, you already collected €$3,000 for him. Brick's €$5,000 bounty only pays if you kill him with the detonator; if you let him live, there is none.

Don't count on item duplication tricks: none is confirmed for 2.5.

title: Watson's ripperdocs all sell the same
body:
Watson has five ripperdocs: **Viktor Vektor** (Little China), **Charles Bucks**, **Dr. Chrome** (Robert Rainwater) and **Instant Implants** (Sogo Watanabe) in Kabuki, and **Cassius Ryder** (Northside, Pershing St.). Viktor won't serve you until you pay his debt.

- **Since 2.0 they all have the same stock at the same prices.** No need to shop around: what they sell depends on your level and on owning Phantom Liberty. If an old guide says each one sells different parts, it predates 2.0.
- Stock refreshes **every 10 levels**, not every 24 hours; the random bonuses you see stay the same until then.
- You can only install or swap cyberware at a ripperdoc.
- **Charles Bucks** gives you a **permanent 20% discount** if you accept his bribe in the gig Last Login (Kabuki, tier 5: steal Alois Daquin's laptop; €$6,400, 1,000 XP and 770 Street Cred). Refuse and he flees; attack or kill him and you lose him as a vendor for good.
- Street Cred also gives a permanent vendor discount: up to 15% at 50, the maximum.

title: Double jump: Reinforced Tendons from level 10
body:
Reinforced Tendons goes in the **Legs** slot: press jump in midair to **double jump**. It costs 8 capacity and is attuned to Reflexes (Crit Chance). Double jump is disabled after falling from too high.

- **Where:** any ripperdoc (all five in Watson), **starting at level 10**; its lowest quality is Tier 2. Sources list no Street Cred requirement.
- **Price:** guides disagree and none gives the 2.5 price. **Check it in game when you reach level 10**, and expect it to cost tens of thousands of eddies.
- 2.x build guides call it the best leg cyberware; both the netrunner and the smart-weapon builds use it.

Alternatives, also Legs and from level 10:
- **Lynx Paws** (capacity 5, attuned to Cool): you move 50% more quietly, faster while crouched, and take −20% fall damage. The stealth option.
- **Fortified Ankles** (capacity 6, attuned to Body): charge jump.

title: Viktor's debt: €$21,000, no deadline
body:
If you didn't pay (or couldn't) in The Ripperdoc, the job **Paid in Full** opens: you owe **Viktor** **€$21,000** for the Ballistic Coprocessor, Basic Kiroshi Optics and Subdermal Armor he installed.

- **There is no deadline.**
- **Until you pay him, his services stay locked.**
- When you have the money, go back to his clinic in Little China. Viktor will try to refuse it and V will insist.

Since in 2.x every ripperdoc sells the same stock at the same price, the debt costs you almost nothing: buy from Charles Bucks, Dr. Chrome, Instant Implants or Cassius Ryder, and pay Viktor when you have €$21,000 to spare.

**Don't pay him before buying what you need**, such as Reinforced Tendons at level 10, if you are short on eddies.

title: Your first cyberdeck and your eyes
body:
**You already have a cyberdeck:** a Tier 1 **Militech Paraline**, since The Rescue. These are sold at any ripperdoc:

- **Militech Paraline:** +10% quickhack damage from Tier 2; from Tier 4, shooting with a smart weapon speeds up a quickhack upload. The one that fits smart weapons.
- **Arasaka:** enemies take longer to trace you; the best for stealth.
- **Tetratronic Rippler:** the one that can reach the most RAM (5 to 20 depending on its tier).
- **Biotech Σ:** from level 10; longer Combat quickhacks and stronger damage over time.

**Eyes:** you already wear Basic Kiroshi Optics (part of Viktor's debt, attuned to Cool). The cheap upgrade for a hacker is **Kiroshi "Sentry" Optics**: Tier 1, capacity 2, **attuned to Intelligence**, and they highlight cameras and turrets when you scan. You have a single Face slot until Birds with Broken Wings (Phantom Liberty).

For more RAM, in the Frontal Cortex: RAM Upgrade (Tier 1) and Memory Boost (from level 5).

title: Free items you can get now
body:
- **Dying Night** (iconic Power pistol): free from Robert Wilson at 2nd Amendment, Megabuilding H10 (job The Gun).
- **Ping** (quickhack): free from Yoko Tsuru at the EdgeNet shop in Kabuki Market (job The Gift).
- **Synapse Burnout** (Tier 3 Combat quickhack): from The Pickup, if you breached the Militech shard and copied the infected data. It costs 10 RAM and your Tier 1 Paraline has 5 base RAM: keep it until you have more RAM (Intelligence, Frontal Cortex cyberware, another deck) or Overclock, at Intelligence 15.
- **Chaos** (iconic Tech pistol): only if Royce died in The Pickup. Brick can only be freed on paths 3 and 4, so if you saved him you most likely have it already.

**In The Heist** you will find **Kongou** (iconic Power pistol), **Satori** (iconic katana) and **Nehan** (iconic throwing knife). **They are missable.** With Phantom Liberty, Herold Lowe sells them later, but don't rely on it: save first and look for them.

title: Skippy waits for Act 2
body:
**Skippy** (iconic smart pistol) lies beside a body in an alley in **Vista del Rey, Heywood**, so you can only fetch it in Act 2. Pick it up as soon as the city opens:

- **It needs no Smart Link** to lock on.
- Choose its mode: **Puppy-Loving Pacifist** (limbs only, non-lethal) or **Stone Cold Killer** (head when you aim).
- For a player with weak aim, it is the best weapon of the early game.
- It doesn't work for dual wielding: Double Trouble only takes Power pistols and revolvers.

**Overture** is not an iconic in 2.x: it is a regular Power revolver that Robert Wilson (Little China) and other vendors stock from level 17.

Jackie's items come after The Heist, and Dex's Plan B after Act 1.

title: Attributes, levels and perk points
body:
- **Six attributes:** Body, Reflexes, Technical Ability, Intelligence, Cool and **Relic** (Phantom Liberty only).
- At character creation you have 3 in each and 7 points to place (max 6 at creation). After that, the cap is **20**.
- **Every level gives +1 attribute point and +1 perk point.** Each skill also gives +1 perk point at its levels 15 and 35.
- **Level cap: 60** with Phantom Liberty, included in the Ultimate Edition (50 without it).

What each point gives: Body +2 max Health; Reflexes +0.5% Crit Chance; Technical Ability +2 Armor; Intelligence +1 max RAM per 4 points; Cool +1.25% Crit Damage.

Since 2.0 cyberware is **attuned to an attribute**: the higher that attribute, the stronger its bonus. Smart Link and Kiroshi "Sentry" Optics, for example, go with Intelligence.

**Skills** (Headhunter, Netrunner, Shinobi, Solo, Engineer) level by use up to 60, independent of the attribute. Netrunner levels with quickhacks, daemons, Smart-weapon or Monowire kills and crafting quickhacks; it gives +1 RAM at its levels 10 and 30.

title: The Intelligence tree for a hacker
body:
The milestones that matter, by Intelligence level:

- **Intelligence 4:** Optimization (+35% RAM recovery), which opens Proximate Propagation, Encryption (−30% traceability) and Subordination. Separately, Eye In The Sky highlights access points and cameras and makes quickhacks sent through cameras cheaper.
- **Intelligence 9:** **Hack Queue**: +1 RAM and, at its second level, **queues: two quickhacks in a row on the same enemy**. **Embedded Exploit**, which needs Optimization: **+60% quickhack damage** against targets under Control, Covert or Distract quickhacks. From it come Shadowrunner, ICEpick, System Overwhelm and Speculation.
- **Intelligence 15:** **Overclock**, which needs Embedded Exploit: you cast quickhacks without enough RAM, and each missing RAM unit costs 10 Health; it lasts 14 s with a 30 s cooldown. It needs a cyberdeck. **Queue Acceleration** adds one more quickhack to the queue.
- **Intelligence 20:** **Spillover** (while Overclock is active, +50% chance for a quickhack to spread to another target), **Queue Mastery** and Smart Synergy.

For RAM recovery: Optimization, Embedded Exploit, Feedback Loop, the Netrunner skill, RAM Upgrade, Memory Boost and Feen-X.

title: Technical Ability and cyberware capacity
body:
**Cyberware Capacity** comes mainly from your level: 24 at level 1, +3 per level, 201 at 60. Capacity Shards, the Engineer skill, Edgerunner and the Chrome Compressor add more. The cyberware perks are in **Technical Ability**:

- **Technical Ability 9: All Things Cyber**: +10% to all your cyberware's stats and −20% capacity cost for Integumentary and Skeleton cyberware. From it: Driver Update (+1 stat modifier on every implant), Chipware Connoisseur and Renaissance Punk (+4 capacity per attribute at 9 or higher).
- **Technical Ability 15: License To Chrome**: +10% cyberware stats, +40 Armor and a **third Skeleton slot**. And **Ambidextrous**: a **second Hands slot**.
- **Technical Ability 20: Edgerunner**: lets you exceed capacity by up to 50 at −0.5% max Health per point over; kills can trigger Fury (more damage and crits for 12 s).

For healing: Glutton For War (Technical Ability 4) and Health Freak (Technical Ability 9). Since 2.0 health items work on cooldowns.

Cyberware is only installed or upgraded at a ripperdoc, with components.

title: Quickhacks and combos
body:
- **Types:** Combat (damage), Control (disable or distract), Covert (low RAM and rarely traced), Ultimate (the most expensive), Device (built into the cyberdeck) and Vehicle (needs Carhacker).
- **Where to get them:** netrunner vendors (quickhacks and specs), enemy netrunners, Airdrops and the Advanced Datamine in Breach Protocol. Since 2.0 vendors no longer sell quickhack crafting components.
- **Breach Protocol now works on access points only**, not on enemies.

**Combos:**
- **Contagion → Overheat:** Contagion poisons and spreads to 2 nearby enemies (4 from its Tier 3); from its Tier 4, Burn or Overheat detonates it. For groups; it doesn't work on mechs or drones.
- **Stacked Cyberware Malfunction → Short Circuit**, which also hits mechs, drones and turrets harder.
- **Memory Wipe first**, to stop traces.
- Synapse Burnout + Overheat, and Cripple Movement + Cyberware Malfunction.
- For stealth, the untraceable ones: System Collapse, Memory Wipe and Sonic Shock.

Note: since 2.02, Tier 5 Memory Wipe costs too much RAM to use.

title: Smart weapons and Smart Link
body:
**Smart weapons** fire guided rounds that **lock on and seek** targets inside the weapon's tracking box: they curve around obstacles and travel slower than normal bullets. Hits are not guaranteed; a better Smart Link tracks better. They take no suppressors or scopes, and Tyger Claws' masking-ink tattoos give smart rounds a 50% miss chance.

- **In 2.x, Smart Link is still required** to lock on. The exception is **Skippy**, which doesn't need it.
- Smart Link goes in the **Hands** slot: Tier 1, capacity 4, attuned to Intelligence, +1 or +2 max RAM. Any ripperdoc sells it.
- **It shares the single Hands slot with the Ballistic Coprocessor** Viktor installed: you have to swap one for the other until you have Ambidextrous (Technical Ability 15).
- Since 2.0 they deal less damage, but they have their own Intelligence branch: Acquisition Specialist, Target Lock Transfer, Targeting Prism (multiple targets when aiming) and Smart Synergy (instant lock during Overclock).
- Without those perks, reloading or switching weapons can break the lock.
- Tier 3 Ping: +25% lock-on speed against pinged targets.

With smart SMGs and pistols plus quickhacks, you barely have to aim.

title: Two pistols with Double Trouble (2.5)
body:
Update 2.5 added **Double Trouble**, a **Cool 9** perk with no prerequisite perk.

- **Power pistols and revolvers only.** It doesn't work with Tech or smart weapons (not Skippy, not King's Coronation), other weapon types, or melee.
- **Level 1:** you carry two guns that fire together, at **−37.5% damage each**; when aiming, −15% recoil and spread.
- **Level 2:** Heywood Hurricane replaces Quick Melee: it fires both guns for 1 s at +50% spread and refunds the ammo of hits.
- **How to equip them:** once it's unlocked, the inventory offers to equip a secondary weapon next to the primary pistol or revolver.
- **Support perks** (Cool 9, need Double Trouble): Two Right Hands, Triple Tequila, Splash Of Love and Keep 'Em Comin'.

IGN's pairings: Riskit and Death and Taxes, Seraph and Unity, Her Majesty and Mancinella. From Act 1 you have Dying Night and Kongou at hand.

The Hurricane fires from the hip and needs little aim, but it uses no smart rounds: for a hacker it is an extra, not the core of the build.

title: How to redistribute perks and attributes
body:
- **Perks:** you refund them **for free, any time, one by one**. There is no button to refund them all at once.
- **Attributes:** there is **one reset per playthrough**, with the Reset Attributes button in the Character screen; you don't need Phantom Liberty. Sources don't fully agree on whether it is offered in every playthrough, so treat it as a one-time chance.
- **Skills:** no source mentions a way to reset them.

**Make a manual save before resetting attributes.** If the new spread doesn't convince you, reload and think it over.

Try perks freely, since refunding them costs nothing, and keep the attribute reset for a big build change, for example from netrunner to smart weapons.

If an old guide says resetting costs eddies or mentions the Tabula e-Rasa shard, that information predates 2.0.

title: The Relic tree (Phantom Liberty)
body:
The **Relic** tree unlocks on its own in **Dog Eat Dog**, when Songbird gives V new Militech software. Dog Eat Dog starts after Transmission, in Act 2: **it doesn't matter before The Heist**.

**15 Relic points:** 3 in Dog Eat Dog, 3 in Birds with Broken Wings and 9 from the Operational and Restricted Data Terminals in Dogtown.

- **Jailbreak:** new abilities for arm cyberware; with the Monowire, it lets it carry a Control quickhack.
- **Data Tunneling** (needs Jailbreak and the Monowire): Monowire hits spread its quickhack.
- **Emergency Cloaking:** Optical Camo in combat makes enemies lose you. Next is **Sensory Protocol**: when you are detected while crouched, time slows so you can escape.
- **Vulnerability Analytics:** shows weak spots on armor and cyberware. Next is Machine Learning.
- Others depend on a specific arm: Projectile Launch System, Gorilla Arms or Mantis Blades.

Netrunner order per game8: Jailbreak → Data Tunneling → Emergency Cloaking → Sensory Protocol → Vulnerability Analytics → Machine Learning. For smart weapons, Vulnerability Analytics and Machine Learning first.

title: Build: quickhack netrunner
body:
Quickhacks do the damage; the gun only finishes. Attributes per game8 (Body / Reflexes / Technical Ability / Intelligence / Cool):

- Level 1: 3 / 4 / 6 / 6 / 3. Level 10: 3 / 7 / 9 / 9 / 3.
- Level 50: 6 / 15 / 15 / 20 / 15. Level 60: 16 / 15 / 15 / 20 / 15 (the Phantom Liberty points into Body). IGN prefers Cool 20 and Body 11 at 60.

**Levels 1–15:** Intelligence 9 first (Hack Queue, Embedded Exploit), Technical Ability 9 (All Things Cyber), Reflexes toward 9 (Dash). Kiroshi "Sentry" Optics, RAM Upgrade, Memory Boost and Smart Link; Paraline or Tetratronic Rippler. Short Circuit, Overheat, Reboot Optics, Ping, and Synapse Burnout once your RAM allows.

**Levels 15–30:** Intelligence 15 (Overclock, Queue Acceleration), Technical Ability 15 (License To Chrome). Contagion; Ex-Disk at 20; Raven Microcyber from 20 if you want spread.

**Levels 30–60:** Intelligence 20 (Queue Mastery, Spillover). Camillo RAM Manager and Pain Editor (30+), NetWatch Netdriver (40+), Cyberpsychosis and System Collapse, and Relic.

**How to play:** open with Overclock; Blood Daemon, Sublimation and Power Surge keep you alive; the Monowire, with Siphon and Live Wire, gives RAM back; finish off with smart weapons (Genjiroh, Prototype: Shingen Mark V).

title: Build: stealth netrunner
body:
No guide has this exact build: it is the netrunner build, which already rewards staying undetected, plus stealth perks and cyberware. Play slow.

- **Attributes:** as the netrunner, but raise Cool earlier, to 15 for Ninjutsu. IGN's spread with Cool 20 fits.
- **Intelligence:** Encryption (−30% traceability), Eye In The Sky (cheaper, longer camera hacks), Embedded Exploit, Subordination and Shadowrunner (takedowns wipe trace).
- **Cool:** Feline Footwork (Cool 4), Killer Instinct (+25% damage out of combat with silenced guns, knives and axes), Ninjutsu (Cool 15), Creeping Death and Vanishing Act (automatic Optical Camo when crouch-sprinting or sliding).
- **Cyberware:** Arasaka cyberdeck (slower traces, −2 RAM for Covert quickhacks, +5 RAM per takedown); Basic Kiroshi Optics or Kiroshi "Sentry" Optics for cameras; Optical Camo and Synaptic Accelerator (slows time at 50% detection), both from level 10; Lynx Paws.
- **Quickhacks:** Memory Wipe, System Collapse, Sonic Shock, Reboot Optics and Ping.
- **Relic:** Emergency Cloaking → Sensory Protocol.

**Levels 1–15:** Intelligence 9, Feline Footwork and, at level 10, Optical Camo, Synaptic Accelerator and Lynx Paws. **15–30:** Ninjutsu and Intelligence 15. **30–60:** Intelligence 20, Cool toward 20 and Relic.

title: Build: smart-weapon gunner
body:
The most forgiving one for weak aim: the gun locks on and you just shoot. Attributes per game8 (Body / Reflexes / Technical Ability / Intelligence / Cool):

- Level 1: 3 / 6 / 4 / 6 / 3. Level 10: 3 / 9 / 4 / 12 / 3.
- Level 50: 15 / 20 / 13 / 20 / 3. Level 60: 18 / 20 / 20 / 20 / 3.

**Levels 1–15:** Smart Link right away; Intelligence from 9 to 12 by level 10; Reflexes 9 for Dash; Body 4 for Painkiller. Acquisition Specialist needs Intelligence 15, so early on you only have base lock-on. Skippy as soon as Act 2 starts.

**Levels 15–30:** Intelligence 15 (Acquisition Specialist, Target Lock Transfer, Targeting Prism, Overclock); Reflexes toward 20.

**Levels 30–60:** Intelligence 20 (Smart Synergy, Spillover), Reflexes 20 (Submachine Fun: switching SMGs auto-reloads) and Technical Ability with the Phantom Liberty points (License To Chrome, Edgerunner).

**Cyberware:** Militech Paraline, **Smart Link (required)**, Kiroshi "The Oracle" Optics, Reinforced Tendons, Ex-Disk + Memory Boost + RAM Upgrade and Electrifying Monowire.

**Weapons and quickhacks:** Yinglong and Prototype: Shingen Mark V, swapping between them for Submachine Fun; Divided We Stand; with Phantom Liberty, Pizdets and Hercules 3AX. Weapon Glitch, Ping (Tier 3 locks faster) and Short Circuit with the electric Yinglong.

title: Switch 2: settings if aiming is hard
body:
The Switch 2 version has **gyro aiming** (Gyroscope Mode), mouse controls and the **touch screen** for menus, skills and Breach Protocol.

- Ranged **Aim Assist**: pick **Substantial**, the highest (Off / Light / Standard / Substantial). Also turn on **Snap to Target**, which snaps to targets when you aim with firearms. Since 2.1 they are in the Accessibility tab.
- **Gyro:** set it to activate only while aiming, lower the sensitivity and use movement dampening.
- Raise **Zoom Sensitivity Reduction** so the camera moves slower while aiming.
- **Breach Protocol:** since 2.1 you can **turn off its timer** (Accessibility), and on Switch 2 you play it by touch.
- **Performance** mode (40 fps) in handheld, or docked on a 120 Hz display, for smoother gyro tracking.
- You can change the difficulty any time.

Play the hacker to aim less: a quickhack only needs a scan and a pick, and smart weapons with Smart Link do the aiming for you. Avoid headshot builds with Deadeye and Focus, which reward precise aim.
